findings.comment: The PR title is "TSL: Introduce `computeKernel()`" and the description explicitly shows usage via `computeUpdate().computeKernel( [ 16, 16, 1 ] )`. However, `computeKernel` is neither declared, exported, nor registered with `addMethodChaining()`. Calling `.computeKernel(...)` will throw a runtime TypeError.

When `compute()` is called before backend initialization, it delegates to `this.computeAsync( computeNodes )`, dropping `dispatchSize`. Furthermore, `computeAsync` has not been updated to accept `dispatchSize` and forward it back to `this.compute()`.
If compute() is called without passing dispatchSize (or if it is passed as undefined/null), indexing dispatchSize[ 0 ] will throw a TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined.

When isValid is false, dispatchSize is reassigned to computeNodeData instead of computeNodeData.dispatchSize. Consequently, computeNodeData.dispatchSize initialized on line 1360 is ignored, dispatchSize.x and dispatchSize.y are set directly on computeNodeData, dispatchSize.y is never set when computeNode.dispatchCount <= maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension, and dispatchSize.z is undefined. This results in passEncoderGPU.dispatchWorkgroups() being called with undefined dimensions.

Strictly requiring workgroupSize to have exactly 3 elements breaks backwards compatibility for any existing code that specifies 1D or 2D workgroup sizes (such as [ 128 ] or [ 16, 16 ]). In WebGPU, workgroup dimensions for Y and Z default to 1 when omitted.
These lines use 4-space indentation instead of tabs, which is inconsistent with the Three.js codebase style.
